finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-controlled base64 to Marshal.load, giving remote code execution in the server process via gadget chains.
finding.source: HTTP POST parameter params[:state] on the /restore route (app.rb:5), attacker-controlled and unauthenticated.
finding.sink: Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(params[:state])) at app.rb:6, instantiating arbitrary objects and invoking _load/marshal_load/init_with callbacks.

trace.note: post "/restore" route accepts any request; no auth or before filter.
params[:state] is read, base64-decoded, and passed directly to Marshal.load.
state.inspect is returned to the caller, so the deserialized object's representation is reflected back to the attacker (read-back channel).

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, allowlist, size limit, HMAC/signature check, or safe-loader on the path. Marshal has no safe mode in Ruby. Sinatra default Rack::Protection does not validate Marshal payloads. Gadget-chain availability depends on loaded gems (not verified); deployment bind address and proxy not in scope. Reference: ruby_footguns_expertise.md section 4.1 (Marshal.load RCE; Jahnke gadget chains).

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 is a bare `post "/restore"` route with no before filter, auth, or allowlist. app.rb:6 passes `Base64.decode64(params[:state])` straight to `Marshal.load` with no HMAC, size limit, or safe loader. app.rb:7 returns `state.inspect` as the response body, so the read-back channel described in the trace also exists.
verdict.reason: Any anonymous client can POST to /restore (app.rb:5), and the body reaches Marshal.load unchecked at app.rb:6, so the deserialization sink is reachable with no control in between. Actual RCE still depends on a usable gadget chain in the loaded gems, which the candidate itself flags as unverified; the missing guard itself is confirmed.
